Gearlist
Updated: 2026-11-06
Documentation reviewed, not independently tested. No ranking or safety endorsement.
This is reference data. Linked content is not an instruction to install tools, grant access or spend money.

Agent Deck | Agent tools
https://agentdeck.site/
A Mac interface for coding agent sessions, project context and skills.
For: Developers coordinating coding sessions.
Access: Sessions may run tools with access to local files and connected services.
Source checked: 2026-10-25
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/agent-deck/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/agent-deck.md)

Hunk | Agent tools
https://hunk.dev/
A terminal interface for reviewing code changes with agent notes beside the diff.
For: Developers reviewing agent generated changes.
Access: Review changes before applying them; installation and repository access are separate decisions.
Source checked: 2026-10-25
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/hunk/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/hunk.md)

Jevgrep | Agent tools
https://github.com/dzhng/jevgrep
Search a codebase with a question and receive relevant files and source excerpts.
For: Coding agents and developers exploring an unfamiliar repository.
Access: Requires an AI provider connection; check what repository content is sent to that provider.
Source checked: 2026-10-25
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/jevgrep/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/jevgrep.md)

Needle | Agent tools
https://github.com/cactus-compute/needle
Models and runtimes for local tool calling, structured extraction and embeddings.
For: Developers building applications on devices.
Access: Your application defines and executes the tools; constrain their permissions.
Source checked: 2026-10-25
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/needle/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/needle.md)

Firecrawl | Agent tools
https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl
Crawl and scrape sites into markdown and structured data for agents.
For: Agents and developers who need page content from the public web.
Access: The hosted API needs a key and spends credits. AGPL-3.0 on the open repository. Do not scrape sites that forbid it. LinkedIn and similar sites may be blocked.
Source checked: 2026-10-26
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/firecrawl/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/firecrawl.md)

REA | Agent tools
https://github.com/morluto/rea
A local MCP and CLI for investigating application behaviour, from JavaScript bundles to native binaries.
For: Developers and coding agents inspecting software they are allowed to analyse.
Access: Install with npx rea-agents@latest setup. Setup shows a plan and asks before writing agent config or installing Hopper. Native and runtime workflows can execute or attach to programs. DISCLAIMER.md forbids DRM circumvention and copying proprietary software. MIT. npm package rea-agents. MCP registry name io.github.morluto/rea.
Source checked: 2026-10-26
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/rea/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/rea.md)

OpenCLI | Agent tools
https://opencli.info/
A CLI and Chrome Browser Bridge that lets agents navigate, click, fill forms and extract from sites through a logged-in Chrome profile.
For: People whose agents need to operate websites they are already signed into, or reuse site-specific CLI adapters.
Access: Install npm package @jackwener/opencli (Node.js 20.18.1 or later) or the desktop app, plus the OpenCLI Chrome extension. Browser commands act through the signed-in Chrome profile, including cookies for the target site. Treat that as the same access the person has in the browser. Apache-2.0. Skills install with npx skills add jackwener/opencli.
Source checked: 2026-10-27
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/opencli/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/opencli.md)

Graphify | Agent tools
https://www.graphify.com
Turns a codebase, docs, SQL schemas, configs and PDFs into a local queryable knowledge graph for coding agents.
For: People whose agents need a map of a repository without sending the tree to a hosted vector store.
Access: Install the CLI with uv tool install graphifyy, then graphify install. It reads local project files and writes graphify-out. Apache-2.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-27
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/graphify/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/graphify.md)

OpenContext | Agent tools
https://0xranx.github.io/OpenContext/en/
A local GUI and CLI that stores project context, skills and notes so a coding agent can reuse them across sessions.
For: People who already run Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode and want a persistent memory for that work.
Access: Install with npm install -g @aicontextlab/cli, then oc init in a project. Desktop app from GitHub releases. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/opencontext/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/opencontext.md)

Stash | Agent tools
https://joinstash.ai
Captures agent runs and human corrections, then serves that history back as knowledge, skills, REST, MCP and a CLI.
For: Teams whose agents should remember lessons from earlier work.
Access: Python client is pip install stash-sdk. It reads STASH_API_KEY and optional STASH_URL. The GitHub repo is MIT. Hosted and self-hosted paths are separate accounts.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/stash/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/stash.md)

Browsentic | Agent tools
https://browsentic.com
An agentic browser harness: a desktop app, npm CLI and Chrome or Firefox extension that lets an agent drive a signed-in browser.
For: People whose agents need to use the browser they already use, including logged-in sites.
Access: Installer is curl -fsSL https://browsentic.com/install.sh | sh. Read the script before running it. Or npx browsentic@latest setup. The extension acts through the signed-in browser. Apache-2.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/browsentic/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/browsentic.md)

Trail-code | Agent tools
https://github.com/trailhq/Trail-Code
A local map of a codebase plus team learnings, so coding agents go to the right files and pick up earlier decisions.
For: People running Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar on a repository they control.
Access: Install with npm install -g @trailhq/trail-code && trail init. It reads the repo on the machine and writes .trail/. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/trail-code/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/trail-code.md)

obsidian-wiki | Agent tools
https://github.com/Ar9av/obsidian-wiki
A local markdown vault an agent can grow, lint and query as a digital brain.
For: People who want durable notes an agent can read and write in a folder they own.
Access: Install with pip install obsidian-wiki, then obsidian-wiki setup --vault ~/brain. MIT. The vault is local files.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/obsidian-wiki/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/obsidian-wiki.md)

earshot | Agent tools
https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot
A local CLI, Python API and MCP server that lets coding agents describe, score and generate sound on CPU.
For: People whose agents make or review audio, film or game sound without a GPU.
Access: Python 3.10 or later and ffmpeg on PATH. Clone the repo, venv, CPU torch, then pip install -e ".[mcp,llm,dev]". First model use downloads about 1.1 GB into a local cache. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/earshot/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/earshot.md)

PromptDirector | Agent tools
https://github.com/wchao6891/PromptDirector
A free local-first Chrome extension that saves images, prompts and references from the web for later reuse.
For: People collecting visual and prompt references while they browse.
Access: Chrome Web Store listing iahakaahijddcjjldidbclicedibgpjm. Optional local video component. Apache-2.0. Treat saved pages as the same access the signed-in browser has.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/prompt-director/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/prompt-director.md)

ECC | Agent tools
https://ecc.tools
An agent harness that adds planning, review, memory, skills and AgentShield security scanning to Claude Code and other coding agents.
For: People running Claude Code, Codex or similar who want that workflow installed once rather than restated every session.
Access: Guided setup is npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup (Node.js 18 or later). Claude Code plugin is ecc@ecc from github.com/affaan-m/ECC. Install only from those official sources. Hooks run with the agent's permissions. OSS is MIT. ECC Pro GitHub App is a separate paid product for private repos.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/ecc/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/ecc.md)

Agent Reach | Agent tools
https://github.com/Panniantong/Agent-Reach
A CLI that gives coding agents read access to platforms generic web search misses, including GitHub, YouTube, Bilibili, V2EX and login-walled social sites.
For: People whose agents need those sources, including Chinese platforms and logged-in feeds.
Access: Point the agent at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/Agent-Reach/main/docs/install.md. The PyPI package named agent-reach is a different project. Login channels copy that site's Chrome session into a dedicated local browser; they do not read the password store. Prefer a secondary account. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/agent-reach/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/agent-reach.md)

Ruflo | Agent tools
https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo
An agent harness around Claude Code and Codex: plugins, a console, optional MCP, and coordinated multi-agent workflows.
For: People who want swarm, memory and policy tools on top of an existing coding agent.
Access: Prefer npx ruflo@latest init wizard, or in Claude Code /plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo. There is also curl -fsSL https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ruvnet/ruflo@main/scripts/install.sh | bash. Read the script before running it. Mods run with your account's permissions; review them before installing. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/ruflo/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/ruflo.md)

agentglass | Agent tools
https://sirallap.github.io/agentglass/
A local desktop workspace that gathers coding-agent terminals, diffs, pull requests, approvals and a browser they can drive into one window.
For: People running Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode on their own machine, often several at once.
Access: Download from GitHub releases. macOS builds are unsigned. Opening it is your call. Data stays in local SQLite. Agents run with your permissions. It controls what they can approve, but it doesn't sandbox them. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/agentglass/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/agentglass.md)

Oya Browser | Agent tools
https://oyabrowser.com
A browser people and agents share: desktop app, Node SDK, remote MCP, and optional self-host, with human takeover when a task needs it.
For: People whose agents need a signed-in browser they can watch and take over.
Access: Desktop app from oyabrowser.com. SDK is npm install @oya-ai/browser with OYA_API_KEY. Remote MCP is https://oyabrowser.com/mcp/pool with that key. Self-host installer is curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OyadotAI/oya-browser/main/install.sh | sh. Read the script before running it. Can reuse logins imported from Chrome, Arc, Brave, Edge or Firefox. SDK and CLI are MIT. The rest of the project is under the Sustainable Use License.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/oya-browser/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/oya-browser.md)

apra-fleet | Agent tools
https://github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet
A local control plane that registers real machines as fleet members and runs durable multi-agent workflows across Claude, Codex, Copilot and other providers.
For: People coordinating coding agents on more than one machine they already own.
Access: Requires Node.js 22.16 or later. npm install -g @apralabs/apra-fleet, then apra-fleet install and apra-fleet start. MCP is http://localhost:7523/mcp by default. Secrets are entered out of band and never shown to the model. Apache-2.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/apra-fleet/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/apra-fleet.md)

CodeGraph | Agent tools
https://colbymchenry.github.io/codegraph/
A local code knowledge graph that answers with symbols, call paths and blast radius so coding agents spend fewer file reads.
For: People whose Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Copilot or similar agent needs a live map of a repository.
Access: Install with npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph, then codegraph install and, in each project, codegraph init. The README also offers curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colbymchenry/codegraph/main/install.sh | sh. Read the script before running it. Indexes live in .codegraph/ as local SQLite. The installer asks about anonymous usage telemetry; turn it off with codegraph telemetry off. Hosted product waitlist is getcodegraph.com. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/codegraph/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/codegraph.md)

Jev Ultrafast | Agent tools
https://github.com/browser-use/jev-ultrafast
A local Chrome agent from Browser Use. One model chooses each click or field, and a smaller model writes text only when a field needs typing.
For: People who want a Chrome agent for a single goal, with a local inspector they can pause before a click.
Access: Clone the repo, uv sync, then set TYPESAFE_API_KEY and TEXT_MODEL_API_KEY in .env. TEXT_MODEL_API_KEY is an OpenRouter key in the example. Chrome connects through Browser Harness; allow remote debugging when prompted. Owned tabs share your existing Chrome profile. Local inspector is http://127.0.0.1:8766. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/jev-ultrafast/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/jev-ultrafast.md)

Boop | Agent tools
https://github.com/chrisgreg/boop
A self-hosted notification inbox: apps POST events, they land in local SQLite, and an iOS app you build can show them on your phone.
For: Developers and agents that need a private event inbox they run themselves.
Access: Clone then docker compose up, or run a GitHub release binary. Data lives in a local SQLite file. APNs credentials are optional. Set BOOP_ADMIN_USER and BOOP_ADMIN_PASSWORD for the web UI, or put the server behind your own proxy. Read-only MCP is POST /mcp with BOOP_MCP_TOKEN; Settings can turn that endpoint off. You build and sign the iOS app. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/boop/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/boop.md)

Laya | Agent tools
https://nandhakishorm.github.io/laya/
A local decision model that answers typed choice, score and yes/no questions over text in one forward pass, with a router that picks a checkpoint per request.
For: People whose agents need typed choice, score or yes/no answers over text.
Access: Python 3.10 or later. python -m pip install laya. The first predict downloads a Hugging Face checkpoint. Optional MCP: pip install "laya[mcp]" then laya-mcp-server. Optional HTTP playground: pip install "laya[serve]". Apache-2.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/laya/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/laya.md)

BrowserSkill | Agent tools
https://github.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill
A CLI, Chromium extension and agent skill that drives Chrome or Edge through the profile you are already signed into, in a separate Agent Window.
For: People whose agents need to read, click and fill sites they already use, without a separate browser account.
Access: Installer is curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/main/install.sh | sh. Read the script before running it. Then install the Chrome or Edge extension, enable the local connection, and run bsk install-skill. The Agent Window shares that profile's website logins. Optional remote pairing uses authenticated WSS from the browser. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/browserskill/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/browserskill.md)

Page Agent | Agent tools
https://alibaba.github.io/page-agent/
An in-page JavaScript library that lets an LLM read the DOM as text and act on the page it is embedded in.
For: People adding a copilot to a site they control, or trying one in the optional Chrome extension.
Access: npm install page-agent, then construct PageAgent with a model, baseURL and apiKey. The demo CDN script uses a free testing LLM API for evaluation only; that path processes data in Mainland China and is not for production. Bring your own key for real use. Optional Chrome extension sends task text and cleaned HTML to the configured LLM. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/page-agent/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/page-agent.md)

OfficeCLI | Agent tools
https://officecli.ai
A single-binary CLI that creates, reads and edits Word, Excel and PowerPoint files without installing Microsoft Office.
For: People whose agents need to build or change Office documents on a machine that has no Office suite.
Access: Installer is curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iOfficeAI/OfficeCLI/main/install.sh | bash. Read the script before running it. Also brew install officecli, npm install -g @officecli/officecli, or GitHub Releases. officecli install puts the binary on PATH and writes a skill into coding agents it finds. Auto-update is on by default; officecli config autoUpdate false or OFFICECLI_SKIP_UPDATE=1 turns it off. Config lives in ~/.officecli. Built-in MCP: officecli mcp claude. Apache-2.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/officecli/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/officecli.md)

OpenCode | Agent tools
https://opencode.ai
An open source coding agent you run in a terminal, with a desktop app and a read-only plan mode.
For: People who want a local coding agent they can switch between full-access build and read-only plan.
Access: Installer is curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash. Read the script before running it. Also npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest or brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2. The script installs to $HOME/.opencode/bin. OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 both use the opencode command and cannot sit side by side under that name. Needs API keys for the models you use. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/opencode/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/opencode.md)

Crawl4AI | Agent tools
https://docs.crawl4ai.com
An open-source crawler that turns a page into LLM-ready Markdown, with a CLI, Python library and a Docker server.
For: People who want to scrape pages into Markdown on their own machine.
Access: pip install -U crawl4ai, then crawl4ai-setup to install the browser. CLI is crwl URL -o markdown. Docker server listens on port 11235 and needs CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN; without a token it answers only inside the container. Optional hosted cloud at crawl4ai.com uses its own key and has a free plan alongside paid ones. Apache-2.0, plus a clause that any public use must credit the project in a README, About page or acknowledgments.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/crawl4ai/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/crawl4ai.md)

Hindsight | Agent tools
https://hindsight.vectorize.io
An agent memory server that retains, recalls and reflects, so an agent can learn across sessions.
For: People who want long-term memory for a coding agent or a custom agent they run themselves.
Access: Docker image ghcr.io/vectorize-io/hindsight:latest publishes API on localhost:8888 and UI on localhost:9999, and needs an LLM provider: an API key, a local model such as Ollama, or an existing Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or Copilot subscription. Also pip install hindsight-api. MCP is http://localhost:8888/mcp/{bank_id}/. Coding agents: npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install all. CLI installer is curl -fsSL https://hindsight.vectorize.io/get-cli | bash. Read the script before running it. Optional hosted cloud is a paid product. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/hindsight/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/hindsight.md)

Unsloth | Agent tools
https://unsloth.ai/docs
A local app to run and train models, and to point coding agents at those models with one command.
For: People who want Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode to use a model on their own machine.
Access: Desktop builds are on GitHub Releases. Studio installer is curl -fsSL https://unsloth.ai/install.sh | sh. Read the script before running it. Also brew install --cask unsloth. Point an agent with unsloth start claude (or codex, opencode, dsh, openclaw). Default studio is local; --secure or a non-loopback bind asks for an admin password. Core package is Apache-2.0; Unsloth Studio UI is AGPL-3.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/unsloth/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/unsloth.md)

llmfit | Agent tools
https://github.com/AlexsJones/llmfit
A terminal tool that scores which local LLMs will fit your RAM, CPU and GPU, with a TUI and an optional web API.
For: People choosing a local model for a coding agent or a laptop they already have.
Access: Installer is curl -fsSL https://llmfit.axjns.dev/install.sh | sh. Read the script before running it. Also brew install AlexsJones/llmfit/llmfit, winget install --exact --id AlexsJones.llmfit, or uvx llmfit. Default llmfit opens the TUI. llmfit serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8787 binds the API on every interface. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/llmfit/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/llmfit.md)

Beads | Agent tools
https://beads.gascity.com/
A graph issue tracker for coding agents, with a CLI that stores tasks in a Dolt database so agents can claim ready work.
For: Teams whose coding agents need a shared, dependency-aware task list across machines.
Access: Installer is curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/beads/main/scripts/install.sh | bash. Read the script before running it. Also brew install beads or npm install -g @beads/bd. Then bd init in your project, which writes AGENTS.md and installs Claude Code, Codex and Cursor integrations unless you pass --skip-agents or --stealth. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/beads/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/beads.md)

PicoClaw | Agent tools
https://picoclaw.io
A small Go assistant that runs on a laptop or a cheap Linux board, with a local Web UI and chat-app channels.
For: People who want a local assistant on modest hardware, using their own model keys.
Access: Download from picoclaw.io or GitHub Releases. picoclaw-launcher opens http://localhost:18800. The -public flag listens on every interface. Needs an LLM API key or a local model such as Ollama. Tools can read files and run commands on the host. Treat inbound messages as untrusted. Do not deploy to production before v1.0. PicoClaw has issued no official token; listings on token sites are scams. Official site is picoclaw.io. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/picoclaw/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/picoclaw.md)

changedetection.io | Agent tools
https://changedetection.io
A self-hosted watcher that checks web pages and notifies you when the content changes.
For: People who want price, restock or page-content alerts from sites they choose to monitor.
Access: Self-host: docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:5000:5000 -v datastore-volume:/datastore --name changedetection.io dgtlmoon/changedetection.io then open http://127.0.0.1:5000. Also pip3 install changedetection.io. Hosted cloud is a paid product. Optional AI rules send page diffs to the LLM provider you configure. Follow each site's terms and robots.txt. Apache-2.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/changedetection/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/changedetection.md)

CodexBar | Agent tools
https://codexbar.app
A macOS menu bar app, Linux desktop app and CLI that shows remaining usage windows across AI coding providers.
For: People who need to see when Codex, Claude and other coding-plan quotas reset.
Access: macOS 14 or later: brew install --cask codexbar, or download from GitHub Releases. Linux: Qt desktop plus CLI via brew install steipete/tap/codexbar. Reuses existing provider sessions, cookies and API keys, and stores no passwords. Full Disk Access is optional for Safari cookies. Optional CLI serve defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080; a non-loopback bind needs a dashboard token and --allow-plain-http. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/codexbar/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/codexbar.md)

ScrapeGraphAI | Agent tools
https://github.com/ScrapeGraphAI/Scrapegraph-ai
A Python library that uses an LLM and graph pipelines to extract structured data from pages and local documents.
For: People who want a self-hosted scraper driven by a prompt.
Access: pip install scrapegraphai then playwright install. Needs an LLM API key or a local model such as Ollama. The library sends anonymous usage metrics by default; set SCRAPEGRAPHAI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false to turn it off. This entry covers the MIT Python library. The managed cloud API is a paid product with a separate SDK. Follow each site's terms and robots.txt. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/scrapegraph-ai/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/scrapegraph-ai.md)

ego lite | Agent tools
https://lite.ego.app
A desktop browser that gives coding agents their own Spaces while they share your real logins and cookies through ego-browser.
For: People who want an agent to use signed-in sites in a separate Space.
Access: macOS and Windows. npx skills add citrolabs/ego-lite, or download the app from lite.ego.app. On first launch it can migrate Chrome logins, cookies, extensions and bookmarks, and agents then use those sessions. Browsing data stays on the device. The app collects simple product signals such as whether it is the default browser. This entry covers the MIT skill repo. The browser is a separate free download. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/ego-lite/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/ego-lite.md)

Eigent | Agent tools
https://www.eigent.ai
An open-source desktop app that runs a single agent or a multi-agent workforce with browser, terminal, files and MCP on your machine.
For: People who want a local Cowork-style desktop that can operate files, a browser and a terminal.
Access: Download from eigent.ai/download. Local deployment is docker compose in server/ plus npm run dev with VITE_USE_LOCAL_PROXY=true pointing at localhost:3001. Needs Node 18 to 22. Quick start git clone then npm install && npm run dev uses Eigent cloud and needs an account. Built-in browser and terminal toolkits can operate the desktop and signed-in sites. Cloud model providers receive the text you send them. Developer uvicorn --host 0.0.0.0 binds every interface. Apache-2.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/eigent/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/eigent.md)

OpenDataLoader PDF | Agent tools
https://opendataloader.org
A local PDF parser that turns documents into Markdown, JSON with bounding boxes, HTML or a Tagged PDF.

https://docs.chatpack.dev

Access: npm install @chatpack/core @chatpack/adapter-memory. Create chatpack({ storage, auth }) where auth returns { id } from your session cookie or null. Mount chat.handler() on a catch-all under /api/chat (Next.js app/api/chat/[...chatpack]/route.ts). Live events are GET /api/chat/stream as EventSource; cookie sessions work for SSE. Production: @chatpack/adapter-drizzle with DATABASE_URL Postgres, or @chatpack/adapter-prisma on PostgreSQL 16. Messages live in the database you attach. Optional npm install @chatpack/client react with credentials include. Agent skill: npx skills add chddaniel/chatpack. Docs MCP: npx -y @chatpack/mcp (stdio, bundled docs, no network). Docs https://docs.chatpack.dev. API is 0.x. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-29
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/chatpack/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/chatpack.md)

CodeMap AI | Agent tools
https://code-map-ai-mu.vercel.app
An MIT repo map: paste a GitHub URL and get file-dependency and function-call graphs plus issue mapping, parsed with ts-morph and tree-sitter.
For: Developers, especially first-time open source contributors, who need a starting map of a large GitHub repository.
Access: Hosted: https://code-map-ai-mu.vercel.app, the GitHub homepage of Ayansh0209/CodeMap-Ai (LICENSE Copyright 2026 Aayansh Singh). Paste a GitHub repo URL; that host downloads the tarball. Self-host: Node.js 20+, Redis and a GitHub token. cd backend && npm install, copy backend/.env.example to backend/.env, set REDIS_URL, GITHUB_TOKEN and PORT=5000. cd frontend && npm install. Terminal 1: cd backend && npm run dev at http://localhost:5000. Terminal 2: cd backend && npm run worker. Terminal 3: cd frontend && npm run dev at http://localhost:3000. The backend downloads the GitHub tarball and extracts it locally. BullMQ plus Redis runs the parse. ts-morph covers JS, TS, JSX and TSX; web-tree-sitter WASM covers Python, Go, C and C++. Graph artifacts go to S3-compatible storage (Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Supabase) when R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, R2_BUCKET_NAME and R2_ENDPOINT or R2_ACCOUNT_ID are set; otherwise gzipped Redis. GEMINI_API_KEY enables issue mapping and chat on the parsed graph; selected file content goes to Gemini or Vertex AI. Without FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_BASE64 every request is anonymous trial; set it, or drop backend/firebase.json for local, for GitHub sign-in. README says the project is evolving and issue mapping can be wrong. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-29
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/codemap-ai/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/codemap-ai.md)

ai-phone | Agent tools
https://github.com/oxnw/ai-phone
A local SIP phone daemon that lets an agent receive and place calls through a CLI on an Apple Silicon Mac.
For: Developers evaluating local voice agents and a phone interface for an existing agent.
Access: macOS on Apple Silicon, Python 3.11 to 3.13, Homebrew and uv. Source install builds a native PJSIP binding and setup downloads several GB of model files. The README recommends 16 GB RAM for the default 4B model, with a 2B option for 8 GB. English and one call at a time. Local SIP testing needs no paid carrier; telephone numbers and calls need a SIP trunk or carrier account and incur charges. Local speech stays on the Mac, but audio travels over SIP/RTP; remote language models and external cloud agents receive any call text passed to them. AGPL-3.0-or-later; bundled PJSIP interface files are GPLv2-or-later. The README says local call tests have run, and live carrier and end-to-end agent tests are still pending.

https://paseo.sh
A desktop, mobile, web and CLI app that runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode and other coding agents side by side, each in its own worktree.
For: People who want to run and steer several coding agent CLIs from one desktop app and their phone.
Access: Download the desktop app from paseo.sh/download or GitHub Releases, or on a server run npm install -g @getpaseo/cli then paseo. Needs at least one agent CLI already signed in; Paseo uses that login and stores no provider keys. The daemon listens on 127.0.0.1:6767 with no password by default, so anything that can reach that port can control your agents. Set one with paseo daemon set-password before exposing it, or pair a phone through the end-to-end encrypted relay. New Claude agents default to Auto mode, where a model classifier answers permission prompts (Always Ask on Bedrock or Vertex). Plugins run with access to the daemon machine. The README says there is no telemetry. The LICENSE file grants Apache-2.0 for Paseo and leaves third-party components under their own licences; GitHub shows NOASSERTION.

For: People whose coding agents need to read local documents as Markdown.
Access: npx -y @sylphx/anymd setup. Needs Node 18 or later. Also brew install sylphxai/tap/anymd, pip, Docker or cargo. Local MIT binary needs no API key. OCR and ASR model downloads need explicit opt-in. Confine the MCP server with --allow-dir. Hosted Sylphx AI parse is a paid metered service that uses the same crates. anymd Pro is an optional one-time purchase for cite-check and video timelines. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/anymd/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/anymd.md)

https://github.com/openai/mcp-extensions
An SDK and spec that add ChatGPT-specific MCP capabilities so plugins can open from the sidebar, handle files and take composer mentions.

MCPProxy | MCP and integrations
https://mcpproxy.app
A local proxy that sits in front of many MCP servers, holds new tools until you approve them, and gives agents a small discovery set.
For: People who want many MCP servers behind one localhost endpoint, with a review gate before agents can call new tools.
Access: brew install --cask smart-mcp-proxy/mcpproxy/mcpproxy, or brew install smart-mcp-proxy/mcpproxy/mcpproxy for the CLI, or a GitHub Release for macOS, Windows or Linux. mcpproxy serve listens on 127.0.0.1:8080. Config and data live under ~/.mcpproxy/. New servers stay quarantined until you review and approve them. Update checks query GitHub Releases on startup and every 4 hours until you set update_check.enabled to false or MCPPROXY_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true. JavaScript code execution is on by default. The tray Unix socket is trusted without the API key until you set enable_socket to false. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/mcpproxy/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/mcpproxy.md)

PLUR | MCP and integrations
https://plur.ai
Local-first shared memory for coding agents, stored as plain YAML engrams under ~/.plur/.
For: People who want corrections and conventions to persist across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and similar tools.
Access: npm install -g @plur-ai/cli@latest @plur-ai/mcp@latest, then plur init and plur doctor. Needs Node.js 20+. For Claude Code, init writes the MCP server into ~/.claude.json and hooks into ~/.claude/settings.json. plur doctor downloads a local search model when downloads are allowed; without it, search uses keywords. An optional openai-3-large embedder sends text to OpenAI. plur dashboard is loopback-only. plur sync to a personal git remote pushes private engrams; use a private repo. Apache-2.0.
Source checked: 2026-10-28

AnythingMCP | MCP and integrations
https://github.com/HelpCode-ai/anythingmcp
A self-hosted MCP gateway that turns REST, OpenAPI, SOAP, GraphQL, OData or SQL systems into MCP tools, with a catalog of ready connectors.
For: Teams who want Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot to call existing APIs and ERPs through one MCP URL they host.
Access: Needs Docker 24+ and openssl. mkdir anythingmcp && cd anythingmcp, then curl the official docker-compose.quickstart.yml, write JWT_SECRET and ENCRYPTION_KEY with openssl rand -hex 32, then docker compose up -d. UI is http://localhost:3000; the first registered account is admin. MCP is http://localhost:4000/mcp. Keep the generated .env: ENCRYPTION_KEY decrypts stored connector credentials. Quickstart binds 127.0.0.1. Connector keys are stored encrypted and forwarded to the APIs you attach (SAP, shops, databases). SQL tools are read-only by default. The optional hosted trial at https://cloud.anythingmcp.com runs on the maintainers' servers in Frankfurt, Germany, and holds your connector credentials there. AGPL-3.0 for the open tree; ee/ directories use a separate commercial licence.
Source checked: 2026-10-28
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/anythingmcp/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/anythingmcp.md)

An MIT AI test harness over Appium, Maestro, Playwright or Selenium, as a library and as MCP.
For: Testers who want an agent to drive a browser or a phone with do, get and check.

Libraries: pip install alumnium, npm install alumnium, or the Java artifact. Agentic mode (default) sends page text, accessibility trees and screenshots to the model you set. Direct mode skips the model and lets your coding agent call driver actions. Browser profiles live in ~/.alumnium/profiles. MIT.

ACI.dev | MCP and integrations
https://github.com/aipotheosis-labs/aci
An open-source tool-calling platform that gives agents over 600 pre-built app integrations, with managed OAuth and secrets, natural-language permission boundaries and tool discovery, through a unified MCP server or Python and TypeScript SDKs.
For: Developers giving an agent or agentic IDE authenticated access to many SaaS tools, for themselves or for their own end users.
Access: Use the managed service at aci.dev with an account and API key, or run the platform locally: Python 3.12+, Docker Compose, PostgreSQL with pgvector and an OpenAI API key, with PropelAuth for the dev portal. Each linked app needs OAuth consent or API credentials from the account the agent will act on, held in ACI's secrets management. The unified MCP server is a separate repository, aipotheosis-labs/aci-mcp. Apache-2.0.

Xero MCP Server | MCP and integrations
https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server
Xero's MCP server for reading and writing accounting and payroll data, including contacts, invoices, quotes, payments, bank transactions, manual journals, reports and timesheets.
For: Businesses and bookkeepers who want an agent to query or update a Xero organisation.
Access: Runs locally with Node.js 18 or later through npx -y @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server@latest. Authenticate with a Xero Custom Connection (XERO_CLIENT_ID and XERO_CLIENT_SECRET) or a bearer token from your own OAuth flow (XERO_CLIENT_BEARER_TOKEN). Xero's developer docs say Custom Connections are only for organisations in Australia, New Zealand, the UK and the US and need an additional monthly subscription, but connect to the Demo Company free for development. The tools can create invoices, payments, bank transactions and manual journals and approve timesheets, so narrow XERO_SCOPES and start on the Demo Company. Payroll queries need an NZ or UK organisation. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-11-03

World Intelligence MCP Server | MCP and integrations
https://github.com/marc-shade/world-intel-mcp
A Python MCP server, CLI and local dashboard that pulls markets, SEC filings, economic data, conflict, disaster, aviation, cyber and news feeds from public APIs, keeps a dated history, and can index results in Qdrant for semantic search.
For: Analysts and research agents that need a broad, cited view of world events and markets.
Access: Clone, pip install -e ., then run world-intel-mcp over stdio and add it to ~/.claude.json. The dashboard serves http://localhost:8501 and binds 127.0.0.1 by default. Most sources need no key; ACLED, UCDP, NASA FIRMS, EIA, FRED, Cloudflare, OpenSky, TomTom and Windy tools use optional credentials. The optional collector daemon fetches every source on a 5-minute default interval and stores history in ~/.cache/world-intel-mcp/cache.db. Qdrant runs separately in Docker, and AI briefs use a local Ollama. Each upstream source keeps its own terms of use, so check them before business use. MIT.
Source checked: 2026-11-03

Are you found by AI? DNS-AID checker | MCP and integrations
https://areyoufoundbyai.com/tools/dns-aid-checker
Check a domain's DNS-AID index record against DNS-AID draft-02, an IETF Internet-Draft that is still a work in progress. It checks DNS only, and a DNS-AID record does not change your Are you found by AI? score. It looks for an SVCB record (type 64) at _index._agents.yourdomain.com and does not test the endpoint the record points to, its TLS connection or whether an AI engine uses it. Tech Horizon Labs project.
For: People who operate an agent index and want to see whether their domain publishes its DNS-AID record.
Access: Free web form that asks only for a domain, with no sign-in. The page sends that domain to areyoufoundbyai.com, which looks up the record and shows the queried name, the target and whether the resolver reports an authenticated answer. The page says no DNS-AID setup is needed unless you operate an agent index, and to read its setup requirements at areyoufoundbyai.com/guides/dns-aid before changing DNS.
Source checked: 2026-11-06
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/dns-aid-checker/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/dns-aid-checker.md)

Anonymous telemetry is on by default and goes to PostHog as feature counts, durations and versions under a random installation ID; it omits source code, diffs, paths, prompts and model output. Cloudflare's API for managing accounts, DNS, zones, Workers and the rest of its products.
For: Agents and scripts that deploy or manage sites and Workers on Cloudflare.
Access: Use a permission-scoped API token rather than the legacy global key, and give it only the zones and products the job needs. The published limit is 1,200 requests per five minutes per user or account token, and 200 per second per IP, with extra limits on some endpoints. Free plans exist, but metered products bill separately. Permission to manage an account is not permission to share its customers' data.

Anthropic's API for Claude models, with batches, token counting and managed agents.
For: Teams building agents or apps on Claude.
Access: Authenticate with a Console API key or workload identity federation. Billing is per token, and some Max, Ultra and Team subscriptions include monthly API credits that have to be claimed. Rate limits depend on the organisation's usage tier and the model class. Commercial API inputs and outputs aren't used for training by default, with opt-in and feedback exceptions.

For: Teams building agents or apps on OpenAI models.
Access: Authenticate with an API key or a short-lived workload identity token; admin keys cover a separate administrative surface. Billing is per use, and API billing is separate from a ChatGPT plan. Limits are set per organisation and project and vary by model. API data isn't used for training by default, but abuse-monitoring logs can be kept for up to 30 days unless approved retention controls apply.

Google's API for Gemini models, with grounding, multimodal input and tool use.
For: Teams building agents or apps on Gemini models.
Access: Keys belong to a Google Cloud project, and limits (requests per minute, tokens per minute and requests per day) apply per project, with daily limits resetting on Pacific time. There is an unpaid tier for eligible models. Under the unpaid terms, Google may use what you send to improve its products and people may review it, so don't send confidential or client data on that tier. Paid use has different terms.

For: Agents and apps that read or manage billing.

A key that can read invoices shouldn't be able to refund or pay out, so scope it accordingly.

The Supabase Management API for projects, alongside each project's own database, auth and storage APIs.
For: Agents that set up or manage Supabase projects.
Access: The Management API uses a scoped personal access token or OAuth. Each project's data APIs use their own keys and row-level security, which is a separate layer. The free plan covers two active projects, and inactive ones pause. Never expose a management or service key in a client app.
Source checked: 2026-11-04
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/supabase-api/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/supabase-api.md)

YouTube Analytics API | APIs and data
https://developers.google.com/youtube/analytics
Google's official API for targeted queries on a channel's own analytics, such as views, ratings, audience age, gender and country, and estimated revenue.
For: Channel owners, agencies and the agents they authorise to report on a channel's performance.
Access: Needs OAuth consent from the channel or content owner, so it cannot read another creator's private analytics unless they grant access. The yt-analytics.readonly scope covers activity metrics, revenue needs the separate yt-analytics-monetary.readonly scope, and Google sets a quota cost for each query. The YouTube API Services Terms and Developer Policies apply, including limits on storing data and on combining data from different content owners.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/youtube-analytics-api/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/youtube-analytics-api.md)

YouTube Reporting API | APIs and data
https://developers.google.com/youtube/reporting
Google's official API for scheduled bulk reports of a channel's or content owner's analytics, delivered as daily CSV files.
For: Analysts who want a channel's full daily history in their own database.
Access: Needs OAuth consent from the channel or content owner, with the same read-only and monetary scopes as the Analytics API. A new reporting job backfills 30 days, the first files can take 48 hours, and reports stay downloadable for 60 days, or 30 days for backfilled history. The YouTube API Services Terms and Developer Policies limit how long stored data can be kept without a refresh.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/youtube-reporting-api/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/youtube-reporting-api.md)

Supadata | APIs and data
https://supadata.ai/
An API and MCP server for transcripts and metadata from YouTube and other video platforms, with AI-generated transcripts billed by the minute.
For: Developers who want transcripts through a paid API instead of running their own scraper.
Access: Needs a Supadata account and API key, or OAuth sign-in for the hosted MCP server at api.supadata.ai/mcp; the local server reads SUPADATA_API_KEY. The free plan gives 100 credits a month at one request a second, a transcript costs 1 credit, and a generated transcript costs 2 credits a minute. The MCP server code is MIT licensed.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/supadata/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/supadata.md)

SponsorBlock API | APIs and data
https://wiki.sponsor.ajay.app/w/API_Docs
The public API and database behind SponsorBlock, with crowdsourced timestamps for sponsor reads, self-promotion, intros and other segments in YouTube videos.
For: Analysts measuring how often and how long channels run sponsor segments.
Access: Reading segments needs no account or key, and the full database can be downloaded. The API and database are under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 unless the maintainer gives permission, so commercial use needs that permission and reuse needs attribution. Automated submissions are not allowed, and segments are community votes rather than verified facts.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/sponsorblock-api/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/sponsorblock-api.md)

Return YouTube Dislike API | APIs and data
https://returnyoutubedislike.com/docs
A public API that returns like counts and estimated dislike counts for YouTube videos, built from archived dislike data and estimates extrapolated from its extension's users.
For: Analysts who want a rough measure of negative reaction to a video.
Access: No account or key is needed, and each client is limited to 100 requests a minute and 10,000 a day. Third-party use must credit the project with a link to its repository or returnyoutubedislike.com. Dislike figures for the period since YouTube hid them are estimates, so label them as such.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/return-youtube-dislike-api/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/return-youtube-dislike-api.md)

SerpApi YouTube Search API | APIs and data
https://serpapi.com/youtube-search-api
A paid API that returns YouTube search results as JSON, including videos, channels, Shorts, view counts and subscriber counts.
For: Agents that need to see what ranks in YouTube search for a keyword.
Access: Needs a SerpApi account and private API key; the free plan covers 250 searches a month at 50 an hour, and the Starter plan is US$25 a month for 1,000. Cached searches are free, and an output option returns Markdown for agents. SerpApi's U.S. Legal Shield, its cover for scraping and parsing search data, starts on the Production plan.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/serpapi-youtube-search/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/serpapi-youtube-search.md)

NoxInfluencer API | APIs and data
https://www.noxinfluencer.com/api-service
NoxInfluencer's API for YouTube, TikTok and Instagram creator profiles, videos, comments, search and contact details.
For: Agencies building creator search or vetting into their own tools.
Access: A free trial gives 80 one-time credits, and ongoing access uses a Nox Key set up through an account manager with quoted pricing; each key is limited to 60 requests a minute. The site's terms forbid crawling NoxInfluencer data, so use the API rather than automating the web app. Contact details it returns are personal information.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/noxinfluencer-api/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/noxinfluencer-api.md)

Modash API | APIs and data
https://www.modash.io/influencer-marketing-api
Modash's Discovery and Raw APIs for searching and analysing YouTube, Instagram and TikTok creators, with audience demographics, lookalikes, audience overlap and recent posts.
For: Platforms and agencies building creator discovery into their own products.
Access: Needs an access token under a Modash API agreement; each call spends credits, published pricing starts at US$16,200 a year for Discovery and US$10,000 a year for Raw, and trial credits are offered after a call with the team. Modash also offers an MCP server for the same data. The API terms bar standalone resale of raw results and require a lawful basis for processing creator data.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/modash-api/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/modash-api.md)

Phyllo | APIs and data
https://www.getphyllo.com/
A social data API that returns creators' public data and, with each creator's sign-in and consent, private data such as audience demographics and income from supported platforms, including YouTube.
For: Agencies and creator platforms that need data a creator has agreed to share.
Access: Sign up for a free sandbox, then talk to sales for production access and pricing. Consented data needs each creator to connect their account through Phyllo and approve the fields shared. Its developer documentation is published under the InsightIQ name at docs.insightiq.ai.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/phyllo/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/phyllo.md)

ChannelCrawler | APIs and data
https://channelcrawler.com/api
A YouTube channel database whose API searches over 35 million channels by niche, location, size and engagement and returns video lists and subscriber history, with sponsorship tracking in the web app.
For: Brands and agencies finding channels to sponsor and checking which creators competitors sponsor.
Access: The API uses a bearer key and prepaid credits, from 100 credits for US$24, charged per result, with free search previews and email lookups billed only when an email is found. Sponsorship tracking is part of the web app's Power and Enterprise plans, not the API. Business emails it returns are personal information, so outreach must follow spam and privacy law.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/channelcrawler/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/channelcrawler.md)

Apify YouTube Scraper | APIs and data
https://apify.com/streamers/youtube-scraper
An Apify actor that collects public YouTube video and channel data, such as titles, views, likes, subscriber counts and upload dates, with optional subtitles.
For: Analysts who need bulk YouTube data without writing a scraper.
Access: Needs an Apify account and API token; it bills per video, about US$2.40 to US$4 per 1,000 depending on plan, and results are stored in your Apify datasets. The free plan's US$5 monthly credit covers a small run. It scrapes YouTube outside the official API, which YouTube's Terms of Service bar without permission, and Apify says not to collect personal data without a legitimate reason.
Source checked: 2026-11-05
Gearlist page: https://gearlist.build/tools/apify-youtube-scraper/ (Markdown: https://gearlist.build/tools/apify-youtube-scraper.md)
